FIB_PLUS	<p>a090_9b6e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f00;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #864f00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266d41;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266d41;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266d41;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, djr, +++, djr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9e3437;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266d41;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #266d41;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266d41;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2a5bb0;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2a5bb0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e3437;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #106d5b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2a5bb0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2a5bb0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e3437;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3437;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266d41;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #266d41;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266d41;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #156493;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #156493;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. 8px;">9,000</td></tr></table><h6>Question</h6> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the order of the genes and the distances between them. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes J and K is [JK] cM (JK)</li><li>The distance between genes J and N is [JN] cM (JN)</li><li>The distance between genes K and N is [KN] cM (KN)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f00;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #864f00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #106d5b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5446c6;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5446c6;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904620;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #904620;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904620;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #106d5b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #763fa5;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #763fa5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. 8px;">26,400</td></tr></table><h6>Question</h6> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the order of the genes and the distances between them. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes F and M is [FM] cM (FM)</li><li>The distance between genes F and W is [FW] cM (FW)</li><li>The distance between genes M and W is [MW] cM (MW)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. For example, if the gene order is B - A - C, simply write "bac" or "cab".</li></ul></p>	FM	18		FW	32		MW	20		geneorder	fmw	wmf
